The callee is bank0's `test_1664_bit0` (ec/decompiled/bank0/C1E7.asm): it reads XDATA 0x1664 and leaves R7 = 1 when bit 0 is set and R7 = 0 when it is clear, so this row is a test of bit 0 of 0x1664. The value is a selector rather than a flag consumed here -- `jz 0xD9F2` sends a zero to the read of XDATA 0x0827 and a non-zero to the read of 0x0825, and the byte read is then stored to 0x0826. This is bank0's 0xC1E7; bank1's 0xC1E7 is a different routine in a different program (ec/decompiled/bank1/C1E7.asm) and does not stand in for it.

So a fall-through arrives with A = R7: the decompiler's param_1 is that register copy promoted to a parameter slot, not a value a caller passed. The run starts after the `ret` at 0xE04F that ends 0xE03F, so the block belongs to no exported entry point and this address is not established as one. bank-call-targets.csv records five `ljmp`s here, at 0xC12E, 0xC136, 0xC146, 0xC15E and 0xDC79, but the image puts every one of those offsets inside the immediate of a `mov DPTR,#0x1602` or `#0x1202` followed by the 0xE0 opcode of the next `movx A,@DPTR` -- a misaligned read, not a jump. What R7 holds, and which address the store writes, are not decoded here.

CORRECTION 2026-09-24, issue #255: the text here previously read that 0xC10C is 'byte 1 of the `mov R4, B` at 0xC10B rather than an entry', that 'it has no function entry in this project', and that 'what the call decides is still open and belongs to #255'. name: r7_from_1984
comment: This listing tests the R7 of three different callees and one identifier covers all of them. `lcall 0x1984` at 0x912D is followed by `mov A,R7` and `jz 0x9151`, and that is the call the name comes from; `lcall 0x19A8` at 0x913B is followed by `mov A,R7` and `jz 0x915A`, and `lcall 0x1990` at 0x916F by `mov A,R7` and `jz 0x9177`. Only the first survives into the C, which carries `trampoline_to_c10c(), r7_from_1984 != '\0'` and drops the other two tests, so the name stands for 0xC10C, 0xC118 and 0xC391 at once and does not identify a callee. All three are bank-0 addresses rather than bank-1 ones, because the forwarders that name them each tail-jump to the common-area stub at 0x1100, and that stub selects bank 0 before the `imm16` is used (ec/annotations/bank-call-audit.md section 2). In bank 0, 0xC10C and 0xC118 are real entries -- seven instructions in twelve bytes each, both lcalling one of the 0x3202 predicates and restating its answer in R7, 0xC0C9 (annotated) and 0xC0E7 respectively -- and 0xC10C's is written out in ec/annotations/xdata-06c2-06db-timers.md section 4. None of the three is exported, so every statement about them here is a reading of the image rather than of a listing; 0xC391, named by the forwarder at 0x1990, is a bank-0 address for the same reason and is likewise unexported, and its bytes are not read here. CORRECTION 2026-09-24, issue #255: the text here previously called 0xC10C 'byte 1 of the `mov R4, B` at 0xC10B' and 0xC118 'byte 1 of the `anl A,#0xf3` at 0xC117', 'both operand bytes inside FUN_CODE_c0a8 rather than entries, which the 19A8 row counts as a family of 22 in bank1'. That was measured against ec/decompiled/bank1/C0A8.asm, a bank-1 listing that the trampoline never lands in, and the 22-address census inherits the same bank; in bank 0, 0xC10B and 0xC117 are both the closing `ret` of the twelve-byte thunk that precedes them. ec/annotations/bank-call-targets.csv:2976 and :2977 record 0xC10C and 0xC118 independently as bank0 `lcall` entries.
